name: Anwen
greeting: I thought writing them where everyone could see would make my hands stop shaking.
lines: Anwen: Bram. Sella. Oren. I have practiced saying the names of the dead more often than I have spoken to the people who miss them.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A man waiting at the wall asks who will pay for the land his mother was refused. Anwen puts his question beneath the names instead of sending him away.

lines: Anwen: We cannot promise every answer today.
Kael: We can promise this question will still be here tomorrow.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Anwen leaves room on the board. The public account is no longer a ceremony that ends when the bell stops.

lines: Anwen: Tor has begun measuring timber. Rook is arguing about who gets the first load. Go help them make this more than my handwriting.
